title: Advanced 2 · Hard sync sweeps
text:
Two oscillators on one note. The second one's SYNC input gets the first one's saw: every time the first starts a cycle, the second is forced to start again too. So the second can only repeat at the first one's rate: its pitch is locked to the first, whatever its own tuning. What its tuning changes now is its shape, and so its tone: as it's tuned higher, more of its cycle fits in before the reset, and you hear a tearing, vocal sweep of harmonics. Here an envelope into the second oscillator's FM sweeps its tuning down over each note: that's the classic screaming sync lead.

Try: turn the second oscillator's TUNE slowly with the envelope's cable out (hear the tone change but not the pitch); the envelope's DECAY; the FM amount; an LFO into FM instead (a sync wah); listen to the first oscillator's saw against the second's on the scope.
